points.option_kind: Mixed. Options 0-11 are zdb cascade branches: each executor picks its own target and applies zdb's gates (hold rule, cheese and budget floors, trap caps). Options 12-20 are engine primitives on the front tile. Options 21-38 are parameterised primitives (bite cheese amount, drop direction, transfer amount, disintegrate). Only 21-38 are masked by exact can* checks.

points.fallback_explanation:
cpi-x0 has 62,446 PRE fallbacks out of 650,788 records (9.60%). 56,361 of them are argmax picks.
(1) 56,463 fallbacks (90.4%) are A_THROW picked while carrying nothing. actExec returns false when getCarrying() is null (Baby.java:1935-1936), but actOk offers options 0-20 unconditionally (2056-2057).
Why the net picks THROW: input 32 is the team's rat-trap count (D.java:392). zdb never places rat traps. placeRatTrap appears only at Baby.java:712 (tryRatTrap, called only from actExec at 1959), Baby.java:1980 (X_RAT_TRAP_FWD) and DK.java:614 (the king's net-only A_TRAP_FOE/A_TRAP_FORT, DK.java:518-528; King.java:355). So the column is 0 in all 969,767 teacher-dp2 PRE records checked, and train_dp.py:120-121 gave it sd = 1 with first-layer weights that never received a gradient (|W1| column mean 0.066, against a median of 0.020 over all columns).
In cpi-x0, 91.6% of PRE rows have nRatT > 0 (mean 10.45, max 25). The KING_ACT floor of 0.1 drives this: 51 A_TRAP_* picks per game, against 6.6 in rl-m2, plus the babies' X_RAT_TRAP_FWD floor picks.
Among carry-free rows, the share with argmax THROW rises with nRatT: 0% at 0-4, 0.05% at 5-9, 1.3% at 10-14, 9.1% at 15-19, 26.8% at 20-24 and 75% at 25. These rows sit late in the game (median round 1452).
Zeroing input 32 changes the argmax in 59,354 rows (58,978 go from THROW to PASS) and removes 56,082 of the 56,361 argmax-pick fallbacks. PRE fallback would drop to about 1%.
(2) 3,151 fallbacks (5.0%) are THROW while carrying an enemy, refused by the hold rule (Baby.java:694). The net sees carry age (D.java:347) but not the flight score bs. Argmax picks fail 90.1% of the time at age < 6 and 0.1% at age >= 6.
(3) About 2,830 fallbacks (4.5%) come from floor or low-probability picks of options 1 and 3-20. Each gets about floor/21 (about 150 picks) because none is masked by executability; CAT_TRAP has 327. Argmax CAT_TRAP fails 33.9% of the time, because its gates and geometry are hidden.
rl-m2 it38 shows THROW at 1.4% of PRE picks with fb 0.83. That is consistent with the same mechanism at lower nRatT, but it is unverified because rl-m2's records are not on the box.
points.context_dependence:
A_PASS skips zdb's whole cascade and both promotions (Baby.java:174-185), so promotion needs an explicit CASH_KING or X_BECOME_KING. Those classes are rare: 117 and 374 imitation labels.
THROW mixes throwing, turning toward the throw and refusing. Its outcome depends on carry age and on the flight score, which is not an input.
NAP, BITE_KING, BITE_RAT, X_BITE_FWD and X_CARRY_FWD do not check hostile() (Baby.java:1940-1942, 1960-1967); zdb's cascade does (138-141). A floor-picked enemy bite or grab during coop backstabs. That ends cooperation for the rest of the game (InternalRobot.java:623-625, 643-651; GameWorld.java:425-431) and bans cat traps for the backstabber for 100 rounds (GameWorld.java:420-423).
X_BECOME_KING promotes anywhere (1994-1997), while zdb promotes only on formSite (181-184). CASH_KING acts on last turn's cashSite, because cashTick runs later, at 158.
LAY_LANE uses lane data gathered only in coop (Baby.java:69). The X_*_FWD options act on whatever tile last turn's BABY_FACE, or this turn's turns, left in front. Targets are chosen inside the executors (biteEnemies: king first, then lowest hp, 737-771; tryCarry: highest hp, 519-537), so the same id hits different robots and the net cannot choose the target.
coupling: Action cooldown: any PRE action leaves isActionReady false. POST then does not open (Baby.java:200), and BABY_MOVE digging and aimCarry (583-635) cannot use the action.
Turning: tryThrow (695), biteEnemies (760) and tryBiteCat (809) turn as a side effect. With TURNING_COOLDOWN 10 (GameConstants.java:252), BABY_FACE then stays closed for this turn (Baby.java:229).
carryRound (Baby.java:516, 534, 1966; reset at 53) drives the THROW hold rule (694) and input 13 (D.java:347). BABY_MOVE's aimCarry throws too.
cashSite and cashTick (BABY_COMMS, Baby.java:158, 1600-1652) drive CASH_KING. formSite and the KING_FORM formation (Baby.java:1528-1532) drive the zdb promotion that PASS skips (181-185).

Team trap counts: the babies' X_RAT_TRAP_FWD (1978-1981) and the king's A_TRAP_* (DK.java:518-528, 602-616) feed input 32 of every baby's PRE and POST net. A floor on KING_ACT therefore moves PRE inputs out of distribution.
X_DIRT_PLACE and X_DIRT_REMOVE write Sym.mem (1988, 1992), which tryThrow's blocked-tile test (667-690) and Nav both read.
Backstab is global: a single enemy bite or grab flips G.coop, and with it hostile() (240-242) and the coop input, for every point of both teams.
Deliveries and transfers change raw and stored cheese (economy inputs of all points) and 'delivered' (893, 2021).
points.features:
There are 53 base inputs (D.java:333-424). In order: phase, role, raw cheese, allCheese/10, coop, round/10, hp, hostile, move readiness, turn readiness, moved, why, carry code (346), carry age (347), canThrowRat (348), foes, friends, adjacent enemy counts (adjacent, attackable, grabbable, holding our rat), min hp, king adjacency, attackability and hp, cat presence, distance, adjacency and attackability, own-king distance, king-cat d2, team cat traps, team rat traps (392), BUDGET, lane count, give (400-407), cashSite flags, canBecomeRatKing, nearest enemy and its d2, hunting, facing, front robot code, front can-place and can-remove flags (420-424), team dirt, x, y, W, H.
The pass-3 inputs 53-57 (D.java:426-445: front hp, drop mask, canAttack front, own-king tile d2, trapCode) and the comms block (446) exist only as zero-weight columns in the widened net (dpnet_io.py:246-247), so the frozen net ignores them.
Inputs 0, 10 and 11 are constant at PRE by construction. Input 32 is constant 0 in imitation but live in RL.
points.generalization_proposal:
(1) Now: zero the first-layer weights of every input column that was constant in the imitation data. Do it at export (train_dp.py:120-121) and in widen (dpnet_io.py:215), and patch the current nets (column 32 of points 2 and 3). Audit all 16 points the same way. Measured on cpi-x0: argmax THROW drops from 61,248 to 1,999 rows, and PRE fallback from 9.6% to about 1%.
(2) Exact masks for options 0-20. Split each zdb helper into a side-effect-free plan() and a do(): tryThrow, tryCarry, biteEnemies, tryBiteCat, tryCatTrap, layLane, tryDeliver, cashPromote, tryRatTrap, dropAlly. zdb's cascade calls plan() then do(), so zdb still replays bug-for-bug. actOk offers an option iff plan() finds an action. X_* options use the can* checks D.babyAct already computes (D.java:420-424, 435). Fallback is then zero by construction, and the floor explores only executable options.
(3) Executors do the 'how'; the net decides the 'whether'. Remove the hold rule from the THROW executor, so holding becomes PASS, and add inputs for the best flight score, its direction and the free directions. Turn the CAT_TRAP, LAY_LANE and RAT_TRAP economy gates (TRAP_FLOOR, TRAP_SURPLUS, CAT_LAY_FLOOR, TRAP_CAP) into inputs. Mask enemy-rat bites and grabs while G.coop, or make backstab an explicit option. Make promotions explicit, with an on-formSite input, so that PASS means only 'no action'. zdb labels keep their meaning.
(4) Capability generalization. Replace the front-only X_* options (12-19) and the parameterised 21-34 with verb x 8-direction options acting on me+d: bite, bite with cheese (2-3 levels), grab, throw toward d, drop to d, rat trap, cat trap, place dirt, remove dirt. The executor turns first if needed, and a turn alone counts as executed, like zdb's turnOnly. Add PASS, BECOME_KING and TRANSFER (all, half), about 76 options in total. Use exact masks and per-direction tile inputs (8 directions x about 8 values: occupant type, team, hp and whether it faces us; wall, dirt, trap; cheese; flight score). Map zdb labels to (verb, direction) by recording the helper's chosen target in D.act. PRE and POST keep sharing the layout, with input 0 as the phase. DNet stays a fixed-size MLP.
points.proposal_cost:
(1) About 20 lines of Python plus a one-off net patch. Under half a day, including a rebuild and the 16/16 replay check; frozen-point behaviour changes only in states with own rat traps.
(2) About 200-300 lines in Baby.java (plan/do split, actOk), plus an exact zdb replay (the existing 24/24 harness) and an RL smoke test. 1-2 days.
(3) About 60-100 Java lines and about 6 new D inputs, plus re-imitation of points 2 and 3 (a teacher run of a few hours on the box). 1-2 days.
(4) About 400-600 Java lines (enumeration, inputs, executor, label mapping). D's input width grows by about 64; the Python training scripts change only in widths. Then re-imitation, replay parity, and about 2-5k extra bytecodes per turn (limits are off). 3-5 days.

points.fallback_explanation:
cpi-x0 has 2,887 POST fallbacks out of 635,878 records (0.45%). Only 9 are argmax picks: argmax DELIVER (7,040 rows) fails 0.1% of the time, and argmax NAP, BITE_RAT and BITE_CAT never fail.
2,850 of the fallbacks are floor picks (net probability < 1e-3) of options 0-20. actOk offers these without checking executability (2056-2057). Each gets about floor/21 (about 150 picks) and fails 83-100% of the time, except the front-tile options 16 and 18, which fail 37-41%.
So POST fallback is pure exploration waste: the record's k never ran, zdb's POST cascade ran instead, and the label differs.
The untrained input 32 also sits in this net (|W1| 0.075, nonzero in 92% of POST rows). It causes no fallbacks, but zeroing it turns 1,283 rows (0.2%) from PASS to DELIVER argmax. Because PASS also skips tryDeliver (225), cpi-x0 has about 100 POST turns per game where the imitation net would deliver but holds its cheese.
rl-m2 it38 shows the same pattern (DELIVER 3,132 picks, fb 0.027; THROW 79 picks, fb 0.949).
points.context_dependence:
The option ids are the same as at PRE, but POST runs after the move: the front tile, 'moved' and 'why' (D.java:343-344) refer to the post-move state, and hostile is still the PRE-time value (Baby.java:136).
zdb's POST behaviour differs from its PRE behaviour: no cat-trap branch, layLane only in coop, a throw only if moved and within budget, and tryDeliver always last (209-226). The net's executors drop all of those gates.
CASH_KING is masked except on the cash site (2056-2057).
coupling: Runs after BABY_MOVE (187-195). If digging or aimCarry (583-635) already used the action, POST does not open (200).
BABY_FREE (point 8, Baby.java:199) runs first; a pickup or own-trap removal there uses the action and closes POST.
Turns made by POST bites or throws close BABY_FACE for this turn (229).
DELIVER feeds allCheese, BUDGET and give for every point, and the 'delivered' count (893) that BABY_ROLE uses.
LAY_LANE and CAT_TRAP draw on the same 10 cat traps (TrapType.java:17) as PRE's CAT_TRAP and the king's A_CAT_TRAP (DK.java:562).
The same backstab and trap-count couplings as at PRE.
points.features: Same 53-input layout as PRE (D.java:327: 'shared layout; feature 0 is the phase'). Here the moved and why inputs (343-344) actually vary. Input 32 is untrained, as at PRE. Pass-3 inputs 53-73 have zero weights.
points.missing_information: Same gaps as at PRE. In addition: whether a POST throw without moving, which only the net can do (zdb never does, 210), is ever useful. The fallback labels are not retained.
points.generalization_proposal:
Use the same head and steps as PRE. POST and PRE already share one layout, with input 0 as the phase.
At POST the argmax is already faithful, so step (2), exact masks, removes about 99% of fallbacks, and step (1) restores the 1,283 suppressed DELIVER argmaxes.
Under step (3), turn zdb's POST-only gates into inputs: moved already exists; add bytecodes left if limits are ever turned on; the coop flag already exists for lanes.
Optionally merge PRE and POST into one 'action slot' point that opens whenever the action is ready, before and after the move. The two nets would then share data: POST has most of the DELIVER labels (281k), PRE most of the THROW labels.
points.proposal_cost: Mostly shared with PRE. The POST-specific part is under 50 Java lines, plus re-imitating point 3 together with point 2. Merging PRE and POST into one point is a D point-id and train_dp configuration change of about half a day. It breaks the 16/16 replay identity for points 2 and 3 until they are re-imitated.

points.fallback_explanation:
cpi-x0 has 384 FACE fallbacks out of 349,251 records (0.11%). All of them are floor picks with net probability < 1e-3; no argmax pick ever fell back.
faceOk masks only F_HEARD (Baby.java:2084), so F_SEEN, F_MEMORY and F_GUARD are offered even when their target is null. Their floor picks (about 146, 124 and 126) fail 99%, 96% and 95% of the time (145 + 119 + 120 fallbacks).
When the argmax is a selector, its target always exists, because the inputs carry each target's direction (D.java:477-492).
F_DIR picks never fail: the point opens only when turning is ready (229), and faceExec returns true once the robot faces the direction (2117-2120).
rl-m2 it38 shows the same floor effect.
points.context_dependence:
F_SEEN, F_MEMORY and F_GUARD are relative: one id turns different ways in different states, and does nothing without a target. F_DIR is absolute.
zdb's guardTurn does nothing in coop, while carrying, or when not turning-ready (Baby.java:247), and the label then stays F_NONE. The net's executors have no coop or carry check (2104-2121), so F_SEEN or F_MEMORY can turn the robot in coop or while carrying. F_GUARD cannot, because Nav.guard is null then (113-115).
The facing chosen here takes effect next turn, in four ways:
- It sets the 90-degree vision cone (BABY_RAT, r2 20: engine UnitType.java:5) that all points sense through.
- It decides grab exposure: an enemy can grab a rat that cannot sense it, or one weaker by HEALTH_GRAB_THRESHOLD (RobotControllerImpl.java:1521-1536).
- It fixes the 'front' tile for the X_*_FWD options, canThrowRat and the front inputs (D.java:415-424).
- It sets the strafe cost of the next move (MOVE_STRAFE_COOLDOWN 18, GameConstants.java:100).
FACE opens only if the action points did not already turn, so it is a residual turn.
coupling: It opens only if the turn is still unused. Turns made by tryThrow (695), biteEnemies (760), tryBiteCat (809), or the actExec turn-only successes (1938, 1948, 2079) keep it closed (229).
Nav.guard (Baby.java:113-115) is shared with Nav movement. memoryThreat reads the start-of-turn 'seen' list.
G.facing (2119, 2129) caches the facing for the next turn's movement and action code.
The facing chosen here sets next turn's PRE front tile, both for the inputs (D.java:415-424) and for the X_* executors (Baby.java:1960-1993), and next turn's grab exposure.
points.features: 32 inputs (D.java:462-505; the '(34)' in the comment at D.java:456 is stale). In order: role, round/10, hp, raw cheese, move and action readiness, moved, facing; direction+1 and d2 of the nearest seen enemy baby (477-478); direction+1 and d2 of the remembered threat (486-487); three always-zero 'heard' inputs (489-491), constant in imitation and in RL, hence inert; Nav.guard direction+1 (492); enemy counts in 8 directions (494-495); cat direction+1 (496); x, y, W, H; coop, carry code, guard != null (502-505).
points.generalization_proposal:
Interim: make faceOk per-turn and mask F_SEEN, F_MEMORY and F_GUARD when their target is null. That is about 5 lines and removes all 384 fallbacks without retraining.
Full: make FACE a pure direction choice. The options become 'keep' plus 8 directions (or 7 relative rotations), all executable whenever the point opens, so fallback is 0 by construction. The selectors' information stays as inputs, where it already is (seen, memory and guard directions).
The imitation label becomes the direction guardTurn turned to (me.directionTo(t)), or 'keep' when it did not turn; D.face (D.java:200) would record the direction.
Add inputs for each of the 8 cones: enemy babies (count, nearest d2, whether it faces us), cat, unexplored tiles from Sym.mem, cheese, the own king, and the next move direction. RL can then learn scouting and defensive facing beyond guardTurn.
points.proposal_cost: Interim mask: about 5-10 Java lines and no retraining; it only stops floor picks of target-less selectors. Direction head: about 60-120 Java lines (label remap, per-direction inputs), 40-60 more inputs, re-imitation of point 4 and a replay parity check, about 1 day. About 1-3k bytecodes per turn for the per-direction scans.

cross_cutting: Untrained input columns are a general hazard. train_dp.py:120-121 gives a constant input sd = 1, and because the input is always 0 its first-layer weights never receive a gradient. When RL, floors or other points later make that input vary, the frozen net gets an uncalibrated push. Here the input is 32 (team rat traps) at PRE and POST. zdb never places rat traps (placeRatTrap appears only at Baby.java:712, Baby.java:1980 and DK.java:614, all net-only paths). In cpi-x0 this input causes 90% of PRE fallbacks (THROW with nothing carried) and about 100 suppressed POST deliveries per game. Every point should be audited against its imitation data; constq.py does this for points 2-4. Fix by zeroing such columns at export and in widen (dpnet_io.py:215), or by clamping inputs to the imitation range.

Mask and executor disagree. For options 0-20 of points 2 and 3, actOk (Baby.java:2056-2057) offers every option whether or not its executor can act, and faceOk (2083-2084) does the same for FACE. Exactly-masked options (pass-3 21-38, F_DIR) never fall back. The floor of 0.005 is spread evenly over the offered options, about 150 picks per option per 650k records. rl_train.py uses the fallback flag only for diagnostics (rl_train.py:536-541), so the policy gradient credits a k that never ran. That is harmless while points 2-4 are frozen, but configs/cpi-x0.json lists phase_b_unlocks [[2,3,4],[6],[1]]. Before unlocking them, add exact masks, or relabel or drop fallback records.

Executors embed zdb's 'whether' logic: the THROW hold rule, cheese and budget floors, trap caps, coop-only lanes. The net decides 'whether' without seeing those inputs. The result is systematic fallback (THROW at carry age < 6 falls back 90% of the time), and RL cannot learn to override zdb's gates. Principle for the refactor: executors do the deterministic 'how' (target and geometry), gates become inputs, and the label stays zdb's decision.

Points are coupled through their inputs. Exploration on one point shifts the state distribution that every other point sees. In cpi-x0 the KING_ACT floor of 0.1 gave 51 A_TRAP_FOE/A_TRAP_FORT picks per game, against 6.6 in rl-m2; with the babies' X_RAT_TRAP_FWD floor picks, 91.6% of PRE rows had own rat traps, against 0% in imitation. Floors and unlock schedules should be judged by what they do to the frozen points' inputs. Backstab is the same kind of risk: actExec bites and grabs have no hostile() check, so a floor pick during coop flips coop for both teams for the rest of the game (InternalRobot.java:623-625, 643-651).

A_PASS bundles 'no action' with 'skip the rest of zdb's logic'. That logic includes the promotions at PRE (Baby.java:174-185) and tryDeliver, layLane and the bites at POST (209-226). Once masks are exact and promotions are explicit options, PASS should mean only 'no action'.

Data retention. cpi-x0's raw decision files were deleted after rl_data extraction (games/j*/ keeps only result.json and trace.tsv), and the npz has no label column, so what zdb did on fallback rows cannot be recovered. decisions.read_rl already returns 'label' (decisions.py:97-150); adding it to rl_data's output would make fallback analysis direct. rl-m2's per-record data is also not on the box, so the nRatT explanation of its 1.4% THROW rate is inferred, not measured.
